status: RESEARCH OUTPUT — requires human review before seeding cropRegistry
purpose: FAO-56 sourced irrigation parameters (kcStages, rootDepthM, depletionFraction) for the 9 SPECIALIZED/GENERAL crops. No other registry fields are populated here.

rules.noInventedNumbers: Every numeric value in this file was read from a source that was actually fetched. Nothing is estimated, averaged, rounded or inferred. Fields that could not be sourced are absent and are listed in `gaps`.
rules.citationShape: { org, title, url, accessed, confidence, note }. `sourceRef` is always an ARRAY of that shape, because a single stage draws `days` from FAO-56 Table 11 and `kc` from Table 12.

conventions.developmentKc: FAO-56 publishes Kc for the initial, mid-season and end-of-late-season points only. The crop-development stage is the linear transition between Kc_ini and Kc_mid, so its `kc` is recorded as null and MUST be interpolated by the engine (FAO-56 Eq. 66).
conventions.lateStageKc: The `kc` recorded on the LATE stage is FAO-56's Kc_end — the value at the END of the late season, NOT the average over it. The engine must interpolate Kc_mid -> Kc_end across the late stage, not hold it flat.
conventions.table11RowSelection: Ordered rule, applied identically to all 9 crops: (1) use the row whose Region column names India; (2) otherwise use the row whose Region and Plant Date best match Indian cropping conditions. The rule applied and every alternative row published in Table 11 are recorded per crop under `alternativeRowsInSource` so a reviewer can override.
conventions.rangeValues: Where FAO-56 prints a two-value range in a single cell (e.g. Kc_end '0.90-0.60'), the FIRST published value is recorded and the full published string is kept in `published`. No midpoint or average is ever computed.
conventions.rootDepthLowerBound: Zr is recorded as the LOWER bound of the published range, on the authority of FAO-56 Table 22 footnote 1: 'The smaller values for Zr may be used for irrigation scheduling and the larger values for modeling soil water stress or for rainfed conditions.' This platform schedules irrigation.
conventions.kcIniGroupRows: In FAO-56 Table 12 the Kc_ini column is printed once per crop GROUP heading row (e.g. 'i. Cereals 0.3') and left blank on the individual crop rows beneath it, except where a crop overrides it. Rice is the only one of these nine crops with a Kc_ini printed on its own row (1.05). For the other eight, the group heading value is recorded and the group is named in the citation note.
conventions.depletionFractionEt: All p values are FAO-56's p for ETc ~ 5 mm/day. Table 22 footnote 2 gives the adjustment the engine must apply for other ETc: p = p_table22 + 0.04 * (5 - ETc), p as a fraction and ETc in mm/day.

FAO56_TABLE_11.title: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 — Crop Evapotranspiration, Chapter 6, TABLE 11. Lengths of crop development stages for various planting periods and climatic regions (days)
FAO56_TABLE_11.note: Table caption footnote *: 'Lengths of crop development stages provided in this table are indicative of general conditions, but may vary substantially from region to region, with climate and cropping conditions, and with crop variety. The user is strongly encouraged to obtain appropriate local information.'

FAO56_TABLE_12.title: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 — Crop Evapotranspiration, Chapter 6, TABLE 12. Single (time-averaged) crop coefficients, Kc, and mean maximum plant heights for non stressed, well-managed crops in subhumid climates (RHmin ~ 45%, u2 ~ 2 m/s) for use with the FAO Penman-Monteith ETo
FAO56_TABLE_12.note: Values are for subhumid climate with u2 ~ 2 m/s and RHmin ~ 45%. FAO-56 Eq. 62 adjusts Kc_mid and Kc_end (>0.45) for local climate and crop height; that adjustment is NOT applied in this file.

FAO56_TABLE_22.title: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 — Crop Evapotranspiration, Chapter 8, TABLE 22. Ranges of maximum effective rooting depth (Zr), and soil water depletion fraction for no stress (p), for common crops
FAO56_TABLE_22.note: Footnote 2: 'The values for p apply for ETc ~ 5 mm/day. The value for p can be adjusted for different ETc according to p = p table 22 + 0.04 (5 - ETc) where p is expressed as a fraction and ETc as mm/day.'

gaps.problem: FAO-56 has no Chilli/Chillies entry in Tables 11, 12 or 22. Verified explicitly against the full fetched tables.
gaps.tried: Fetched and parsed the complete raw HTML of both chapters and searched for 'chilli'/'chillies'/'capsicum' — zero hits.
gaps.resolution: All CHILLI values proxied from 'Sweet peppers (bell)' and flagged with `proxy.isProxy: true`. REQUIRES HUMAN APPROVAL, or replacement with an Indian source (e.g. an ICAR/TNAU/state-university package of practices giving a chilli Kc curve).

gaps.field: kcStages[].days — row selection for RICE, COTTON, SOYBEAN, TOMATO, POTATO, ONION, CHILLI
gaps.problem: FAO-56 Table 11 names India only in the wheat row ('Central India') and the maize row ('India (dry, cool)'). For the other seven crops no India row exists, so stage lengths come from a region/plant-date analogue chosen by the documented rule.
gaps.tried: Read every published Table 11 row for all nine crops from the raw HTML; all alternatives are recorded per crop under `alternativeRowsInSource`.
gaps.resolution: Selection is a documented judgement, not a FAO statement. Table 11's own caption footnote says the user is strongly encouraged to obtain local information — Indian state-university or ICAR crop durations should override these before demo. SOYBEAN is the weakest match (85-day Tropics row, Dec plant date vs Indian June-July kharif sowing).

gaps.problem: Table 11 prints Lmid as '30/45' with Total '115/130' against Plant Date 'Jan/Nov'. FAO-56 does not state which length belongs to which planting date.
gaps.tried: Searched Chapter 6 body text and all Table 11 footnotes for a convention explaining slash-separated cells; none found.
gaps.resolution: Recorded 30 (first published value, total 115). Reviewer must decide; if the Nov planting maps to 45, the Indian rabi potato entry should be 130 days.

gaps.problem: FAO-56 publishes distinct Kc_ini and Zr for Winter Wheat (0.4 frozen / 0.7 non-frozen; Zr 1.5-1.8 m) and Spring Wheat (0.3; Zr 1.0-1.5 m). It does not say which applies to Indian rabi wheat.
gaps.tried: Read Table 11 footnote 2 and the Table 12 winter-wheat sub-rows; both condition winter wheat on frozen soils / dormancy / northern temperate planting rules.
gaps.resolution: Spring Wheat selected and the reasoning recorded in `whyThisEntry`; winter-wheat values kept in `alternativeRowsInSource`. p = 0.55 either way, so only Kc_ini and Zr are at stake.

gaps.field: Kc_end for RICE, COTTON, TOMATO (and Kc_mid for COTTON)
gaps.problem: These cells publish a two-value range with NO footnote explaining the split: Rice Kc_end '0.90-0.60', Cotton Kc_mid '1.15-1.20', Cotton Kc_end '0.70-0.50', Tomato Kc_end '0.70-0.90'.
gaps.tried: Read every numbered Table 12 footnote (1-25) from the raw HTML; none attaches to these cells. Searched Chapter 6 body text for rice/cotton Kc_end discussion — only the rice Kc_ini paddy-water passage was found.
gaps.resolution: First published value recorded in each case, with `published` retaining the full string. No midpoint was computed. Rice in particular matters: a drained-before-harvest field and a field kept ponded to harvest are very different, and the platform already flags rice standing-water logic.

gaps.field: Kc_end for WHEAT and MAIZE — footnoted alternatives not applied
gaps.problem: Wheat Kc_end '0.25-0.4', footnote 10: the higher value is for hand-harvested crops. Maize Kc_end '0.60-0.35', footnote 11: the first is for harvest at high grain moisture, the second for harvest after complete field drying (~18% moisture).
gaps.tried: Both footnotes were read in full and are quoted in the citation notes.
gaps.resolution: First published value recorded for consistency. Deciding which Indian practice applies is an agronomic judgement I deliberately did NOT make — it needs the reviewer, since hand harvesting and field-dried grain are both common in India and both would flip the value.

gaps.problem: Table 12 footnote 2 says tomatoes/peppers grown on stalks of 1.5-2 m need increased Kc (1.20 for tomato, 1.15 for peppers), with h increased too. FAO-56 does not say which Indian systems are staked.
gaps.tried: Footnote read in full and quoted in the Kc_mid citation for both crops.
gaps.resolution: Unstaked table values recorded (tomato 1.15, chilli 1.05). Reviewer decides.

gaps.tried: n/a — this is not a sourcing failure.
gaps.resolution: By design: FAO-56 publishes Kc at three points only and defines the development stage as the linear transition (Eq. 66). The engine must interpolate. Recorded as null rather than pre-computed so no invented number enters the data.

gaps.field: rootDepthM — single value from a range
gaps.problem: Table 22 publishes Zr only as a range; no crop has a single published Zr.
gaps.resolution: Lower bound recorded for every crop, on the footnote's own guidance that smaller Zr values are for irrigation scheduling. The full published range is kept in `published` so a reviewer can switch to the upper bound for rainfed/stress modelling.

gaps.problem: Table 22 footnote 4 states the rice p of 0.20 is 'of saturation' — a different reference point from every other crop, where p is a fraction of total available water between field capacity and wilting point.
gaps.tried: Footnote located and quoted verbatim in the citation and in `depletionFraction.caveat`.
gaps.resolution: Recorded with a prominent caveat. This is an engine-correctness hazard, not a data gap: applying rice p through the standard TAW formula would be wrong.

gaps.problem: Table 12 values are for a subhumid climate (RHmin ~ 45%, u2 ~ 2 m/s). Much of India is arid to semi-arid, where FAO-56 Eq. 62 raises Kc_mid materially (FAO-56 Box 14 shows wheat Kc_mid ranging 1.02 to 1.25 by climate and wind).
gaps.tried: Read Box 14 and the climate-classification tables in Chapter 6.
gaps.resolution: NOT applied — Eq. 62 needs per-location RHmin and u2, which is engine input, not registry data. Recorded here so the engine design accounts for it rather than silently under-estimating ETc.
